collection.integrity: Tiles are fetched with no `out` limit, so a tile either arrives whole or fails loudly — there is no silent truncation to detect. One count query per seed box cross-checks the result: seed_cross_checks compares the box total against the distinct cameras its tiles yielded, and a shortfall over 2% aborts the run rather than publishing a partial map.
collection.method: seeded adaptive tiling. Five seed boxes tile the whole planet exactly once; the contiguous states are pre-cut into a 4 x 8 grid. Every tile is COUNTED before it is fetched, and a tile over the element limit — or one that errors — is quartered and each quarter counted in turn.
collection.note: Overpass bounding boxes are inclusive on all four edges, so a camera sitting exactly on a tile line is returned twice. Records are keyed on the OSM object id and deduplicated; duplicates_across_tile_edges is how many were absorbed.
collection.slot_waiting_note: Overpass allocates each IP a small number of execution slots and publishes their availability at /api/status. This collector consults it before every query and waits exactly as long as the server states, rather than guessing at a backoff.

counties_note: Every county in the TIGER roster, including the ones with nothing mapped in them — that is what makes zero renderable. Row shape is [fips, name, state, cameras_mapped].

coverage.not_reconciled_with_vendor_figures: Flock Safety publishes its own deployment figures and they differ from this count. This site does not reconcile the two, because reconciling them would mean imputing cameras nobody has mapped, and this site never imputes.
coverage.what_zero_means: A county with zero mapped cameras is a county nobody has mapped. It is NOT a county with no cameras. This dataset cannot tell those two apart, and neither can anyone reading it: 948 of 3,235 counties are in that state.
coverage.why_it_is_uneven: Coverage follows volunteers, not deployments. A city where a DeFlock contributor has been active looks saturated; an identical city with no contributor looks empty. The difference between them is the contributor.

exactly_zero.caution: A bare direction=0 means due north AND is the value left behind when a bearing was never established. The two cannot be told apart, so the north bin is inflated by an unknown amount. Nothing is reweighted to hide it.

field_of_view.note: Only the sector form states a field of view. Where it does, the width is real; where it does not, no width is inferred. Widths are not carried per camera in flock-points.json — they are aggregate only.

direction.note: The bearing the camera looks along, as tagged. It is the field nobody renders and the one that says most about what a camera is for: an ALPR aimed along a carriageway reads the traffic on it. Cameras with no direction tag are absent from these bins entirely — they are not binned as north.

tag_form_legend.bearing: a plain bearing in degrees, e.g. "142".
tag_form_legend.multi: an OSM multi-value, e.g. "0;0". The first value is used; the others are not averaged in.
tag_form_legend.sector: an OSM field-of-view arc, e.g. "338-23" — 45 degrees wide, centred on 0. The centre is DERIVED, not tagged.

direction.units: degrees clockwise from true north; 0 is due north

geography.label: Census TIGERweb county boundaries
geography.note: county polygons simplified to about 550 m; a site within a few hundred metres of a county line can be assigned to the neighbouring county, and says so

grid.note: Occupied cells only, for the national view. Row shape is [lat_index, lon_index, count]; the cell south-west corner is lat_index * cell_deg, lon_index * cell_deg (WGS84). A cell absent from this array has no MAPPED cameras, which is not the same as none.

honesty: Every figure here counts cameras as mapped in OpenStreetMap on 2026-09-26. It is not a count of cameras that exist.
948 of 3,235 counties have zero mapped cameras. That means nobody has mapped them, not that they have none.
OpenStreetMap coverage is volunteer-driven and uneven; the map is partly a map of where mappers have been.
Direction is tagged on 113,241 of 115,608 cameras. The untagged ones are shown as untagged, never as facing north.

5,741 cameras carry a bare direction=0. That is both "due north" and what a mapper leaves behind when the bearing is unknown, so the north bin is inflated by an amount nobody can measure. It is not reweighted.
An operating agency is recorded for 14,953 of 115,608. For the rest OSM does not say who runs the camera, and neither does this page.
County assignment uses TIGER polygons simplified to about 550 m, so a camera within a few hundred metres of a county line can land in the neighbouring county.
258 mapped cameras fall outside any US county. They are counted and kept, not dropped.
Flock Safety publishes different deployment figures. The two are not reconciled here, because reconciling them would mean imputing.

points_file.note: Flat parallel integer arrays. lat = lat_q / quantisation. dir of -1 means no usable direction tag, NOT north. st indexes that file's own states array, and -1 means the camera is not inside any US county.

source.label: OpenStreetMap ALPR nodes tagged Flock Safety, via Overpass
source.recompute: Substitute a bounding box into query_template and POST it to the endpoint as a form-encoded `data=` field (a raw POST body answers HTTP 406). Every figure on this page is the arithmetic in collector/flock.mjs over that response and nothing else.
